cases.scope: Pinned XStream snapshots, DomDriver, default XStream configuration, untrusted XML requesting a Runnable dynamic proxy with java.beans.EventHandler and a harmless Marker.touch target; the caller would invoke run() only after successful unmarshalling. Both logs show ConversionException and zero callbacks. No root cause or successful proxy construction is recorded. This does not establish advisory callback execution or its prevention by the patch.

Assertion PASS/PASS means only that an XStreamException occurred and callbacks stayed zero. ConversionException cause is absent; this is not evidence of advisory mitigation. A bounded fixture must first demonstrate successful proxy construction and a harmless callback on before, record the exception cause and conversion stage, then evaluate the same input/oracle on after with any security configuration stated explicitly and ordinary controls passing. The pinned patch's setupSecurity adds AnyTypePermission.ANY; new permission APIs alone do not prove default rejection. Map the result to the actual caller and affected callable. No shell execution is needed. Version 1.4.10, JSON and other gadget chains are outside this pair.

cases.upstream_scope_notes: SecurityVulnerabilityTest overrides setupSecurity with an empty method; individual tests can explicitly allow types. In 2020 the explicit EventHandler test also changes converter registration between snapshots, and the new ContainsFilter cases are guarded by JVM.isVersion(7), meaning >= Java 7 (the recorded JDK8 satisfies this check). In 2021 the added tests cover denial and explicit allowance of manipulated ByteArrayInputStream, not the advisory RCE chain.
